battlecards.why_selected: Delivered deepest price concessions (≈20% on full market basket) while eliminating transition risk; agreed to firm two-year pricing and quarterly rebates.
battlecards.contract_terms: 2-year master supply agreement (15-Jul-2024 – 15-Jul-2026) with firm pricing, volume-based rebates, optional 1-year renewal.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Credible threat of switch to Medline/Cardinal, SKU-level benchmark gaps, and consolidated enterprise volume enabled aggressive discounting.
supplier_weaknesses: Only 15 % SKU overlap in initial benchmark required iterative pricing rounds
battlecards.switching_costs: Low-to-moderate since incumbent systems already in place; retaining supplier avoided staff retraining and formulary rebuild.
key_contacts: Shane Holloway – VP Post-Acute Corporate Accounts
battlecards.notes: MOU executed July 2024; savings to be validated quarterly by Treya and Choice Health finance.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Offered only 10 % savings vs. McKesson’s 20 %+ and required full system transition with higher implementation cost.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Used Medline quote as benchmark to secure deeper concessions from incumbent.
supplier_weaknesses: Missed target prices on ~50 % of market basket
Limited EDI readiness for Choice systems
battlecards.switching_costs: High – new ordering portal, SKU cross-referencing, and staff training required.
battlecards.notes: Kept engaged through two RFP rounds; final offer submitted 18-Jun-2024.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Initial submission had unit-of-measure discrepancies; corrected pricing still lagged McKesson on high-volume SKUs and lacked firm rebate commitment.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Incomplete bid limited utility, but presence in final round reinforced competitive tension.
supplier_strengths: Regional DC in Fort Worth (reduced transit times)
supplier_weaknesses: Data quality issues in RFP response
battlecards.switching_costs: Would require new EDI integration and distribution onboarding.
battlecards.notes: Treya analysis indicates potential to revisit in future cycles if service issues with incumbent arise.
complexity_reasons: Bid quality issues required additional analysis

battlecards.why_selected: Amended full-maintenance program cut monthly maintenance rates up to 48 % in low-mileage bucket without disrupting existing leases.
battlecards.contract_terms: Service Agreement Addendum executed Jun-2024; maintenance rates tiered by five mileage buckets; annual review clause.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Treya analysis showed only 33 % of vehicles drew maintenance yet were billed flat rate; data drove cost-to-serve argument.
supplier_weaknesses: Legacy flat-rate model over-billed Choice Health
Limited transparency on pass-through repair costs
battlecards.switching_costs: High – 385 active leases would incur termination penalties; driver onboarding to new lessor.
battlecards.notes: Savings tracked at $140 K annually; Treya to memorialize terms and monitor adherence through quarterly scorecards.
complexity_reasons: Detailed benchmark analysis used to drive pricing
